newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lufthansa transport express shipments on Bordeaux-Munich route.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa transport express shipments on Bordeaux-Munich route.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said its six-times weekly passenger service between Bordeaux and Munich, via Marseille, launched last month, was handling a small quantity of express shipments.

The Canadair Regional Jet (CRJ), which Lufthansa operates on the route offers global belly capacity of around 500 kilos which when luggage is taken into account leaves around 150 kilos for freight, a LHAG cargo official told Reuters.

"We are talking about very limited cargo capacity, which can only accomodate low-volume items. Nevertheless, we have already generated some demand, one example being for aircraft parts, manufactured by Airbus and other aviation suppliers in the Bordeaux region and destined for export," the official said.
A major plus point for the express service was that shipments left Bordeaux on an early morning flight, arriving in Munich by 1015 local time having made a stopover in Marseille.
From Munich, Lufthansa operates a programme of flights to around 80 domestic, European and long-haul destinations.
"We can advise customers on whether it is better to use Munich as a gateway/transhipment point as opposed to Frankfurt or vice versa. All-in-all, Munich provides an extra choice."

On the return leg from Munich, flights arrived at Marseille and Bordeaux at 2020 and 2200 respectively which meant express shipments were available for delivery the following morning, the official added.
Lufthansa had also obtained cabotage rights to transport freight between Bordeaux and Marseille.

"If the Bordeaux-Marseille-Munich service proved to be successful, there might be some scope to create passenger services of this type from French airports with once again a potential spin-off for express shipments."
